name: MemoryAgentBench (Evaluating Memory in LLM Agents via Incremental Multi-Turn Interactions)
venue: arXiv preprint 2507.05257 (cs.CL); accepted as ICLR 2026 Poster (OpenReview forum id=DT7JyQC3MR)
authors_affiliation: Yuanzhe Hu*, Yu Wang* (equal contribution), Julian McAuley. University of California, San Diego (UCSD). Joint corresponding authors: Yuanzhe Hu and Yu Wang.
task_domain: Memory evaluation for LLM agents over multi-turn interactions; spans QA (single-/multi-hop document QA, dialogue-based QA, novel event QA), classification/recommendation (test-time learning), long-document summarization and detective-novel reasoning (long-range understanding), and counterfactual fact updating (selective forgetting). A benchmark + unified evaluation framework rather than a single method.
problem_setting: Interactive, incremental, single-agent (single-user) memory evaluation. Agents receive textual inputs as a sequence of chunks wrapped in a simulated User-Assistant dialogue, each preceded by a memorization instruction; they must absorb and incrementally update memory chunk by chunk, then answer questions only after all chunks are ingested. Contexts range 103K-1.44M tokens, far exceeding typical context windows, forcing genuine memory mechanisms. No task-specific training/supervision is provided (test-time/deployment setting); the benchmark identifies four core competencies (Accurate Retrieval, Test-Time Learning, Long-Range Understanding, Selective Forgetting) and evaluates whether existing memory-agent architectures master them.
what_is_retrieved: Past textual context the agent has ingested: raw input chunks (documents, dialogue turns, labeled in-context examples, novel passages, counterfactual fact-edit pairs) stored in episodic/external memory; for structure-augmented agents, entities/relations in a knowledge graph or tree. This is what the evaluated agents retrieve; the benchmark itself does not retrieve.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes incrementally during the interaction (chunks absorbed one by one and consolidated). It is not a static external corpus; the store is built online from the streamed conversation. (Benchmark evaluates agents over this growing memory.)
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Mixed by competency. RAG/agentic-memory agents use a fixed top-k retrieval objective (k=10 chunks by default; ablated at 2/5/10). The benchmark's design philosophy critiques pure top-k: Long-Range Understanding and Test-Time Learning require holistic/complete-set integration across the entire history that top-k retrieval cannot recover, while Accurate Retrieval needs recovery of the correct (possibly multi-hop) snippet(s). Selective Forgetting requires recovering the single most recent (correct) fact among contradictory edits.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method; it is a benchmark). The evaluated agentic-memory agents loosely realize Retrieve/Reuse but the benchmark does not frame itself in CBR terms.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is grounded instead in memory science and cognitive science (James 1890; McClelland et al. 1995; Anderson & Neely 1996; Wimber et al. 2015).
retrieval_unit: Primarily text chunk / passage (chunk size 512 tokens for SH-Doc QA, MH-Doc QA, LME(S*) and all Selective-Forgetting tasks; 4096 tokens for other tasks and uniformly 4096 for Mem0/Cognee/Zep/MIRIX). Structure-augmented agents additionally retrieve KG-subgraph / tree-node / event-timeline units; long-context agents use the whole context buffer (no retrieval unit).
index_source: Growing memory induced online/test-time: built by segmenting reconstructed long-context datasets into chunks and feeding them incrementally in time order. The benchmark transforms existing long-context datasets (NIAH-style Doc QA, LongMemEval, infinity-Bench Sum, DetectiveQA, classification datasets, MQUAKE edit pairs) and adds two newly constructed datasets (EventQA, FactConsolidation) into the incremental multi-turn format.
index_structure_topology: Depends on the evaluated agent: flat raw-text store (Simple RAG / BM25), flat dense vector index (embedding RAG), knowledge GRAPH (GraphRAG, HippoRAG-v2, Cognee, Zep temporal KG), tree (RAPTOR recursive abstractive tree), event timeline, or hierarchical/multi-agent memory (MemGPT paging, MIRIX multi-component memory). Long-context agents use a FIFO context buffer (no structured index).
retriever_type: Heterogeneous across evaluated agents: lexical/non-neural (BM25), dense/embedding (Contriever, OpenAI text-embedding-3-small/large, Qwen3-Embedding-4B), structure-augmented (GraphRAG, RAPTOR, HippoRAG-v2, MemoRAG), commercial/agentic memory (Mem0, Cognee, Zep, MemGPT, MIRIX, Self-RAG). Long-context agents do not retrieve (full context as memory).
retriever_learning_signal: None / off-the-shelf for the core comparison: retrievers are used as-is (pretrained BM25/embedding models, off-the-shelf graph/commercial memory systems). No retriever is trained or RL-optimized within the benchmark; selection is fixed similarity top-k.
query_construction: Raw user question is used as the query at test time. Agentic memory agents (e.g., Self-RAG, MemGPT) may reformulate the question internally across iterative reasoning cycles; structure-augmented systems may translate queries against a KG/tree. The benchmark itself supplies the raw question.
query_granularity: Task-level (one query per question issued after the full incremental context is ingested). Multiple questions follow a single ingested context (e.g., 5 contexts paired with 300 questions in LongMemEval(S*)) to amortize memory-construction cost. Agentic agents may issue step/iteration-level sub-queries internally.
when_to_retrieve: Two-phase protocol: a memory-construction phase (incremental chunk ingestion, build/update memory) followed by a query-execution phase where retrieval happens at answer time. For most RAG agents this is one-shot retrieval per question; agentic memory agents (MemGPT, Self-RAG) perform iterative/active retrieval loops.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule for RAG agents (retrieve top-k at each question). For agentic memory agents, retrieval is agent-initiated / reflection-driven within iterative reasoning cycles (self-reflection tokens in Self-RAG; function-call/paging decisions in MemGPT). The benchmark does not impose a single trigger; it depends on each agent's design.
reranking: No reranking stage is imposed by the benchmark; RAG agents use plain similarity top-k (default k=10). Some structure-augmented/commercial systems may apply internal ranking, but no dedicated cross-encoder/RRF reranking is reported as a benchmark component.
retrieved_context_refinement: Depends on agent: Simple/embedding RAG inject retrieved chunks verbatim (no refinement). Structure-augmented agents perform summarization/abstraction (RAPTOR recursive summaries, GraphRAG community summaries, MemoRAG global memory draft). Agentic agents (Self-RAG) apply self-reflection/critique filtering. The benchmark itself does not prescribe refinement.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: retrieved chunks / KG-subgraphs / summaries are concatenated into the LLM prompt to answer the question. Long-context agents place the entire (windowed) history in-context. With chunk size 4096 and top-k=10 the injected context is ~40K tokens. No training-signal or latent-token usage.
planning_integration: Mostly retrieve-then-answer (one-shot retrieval at query time, not interleaved with multi-step planning) for RAG agents. Agentic memory agents use an iterative retrieve-reflect-update loop (per-iteration interleaving). No MCTS/tree-search planning is involved; the benchmark targets memorization rather than action planning.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer for long-context and standard RAG agents (single retrieval then generate the answer). Per-iteration / per-reasoning-cycle for agentic memory agents (MemGPT, Self-RAG, MemoRAG) that reformulate, look up memory, and update working memory across cycles.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR method). Retrieved content is used as verbatim in-context evidence (RAG) or, for test-time learning tasks, as labeled in-context exemplars from which the agent must induce the labeling rule; no explicit case revision/critic mechanism is prescribed by the benchmark.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw text chunks (RAG/long-context); for structure-augmented agents, distilled summaries / structured KG facts / tree-node abstractions / event timelines. For Test-Time Learning, raw labeled (input, label) demonstrations. For Selective Forgetting, serial-numbered fact statements.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Spans the spectrum: raw trajectory/passage (RAG, long-context), single demonstration (TTL labeled examples), distilled summary/insight (RAPTOR, GraphRAG, MemoRAG), and structured fact/rule (KG-based Cognee/Zep/HippoRAG, FactConsolidation serial-numbered facts). The benchmark deliberately spans abstraction levels to test whether retrieval-only abstraction suffices.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Not a built-in mechanism but a tested property: the benchmark stresses robustness to distractors (NIAH-style multi-document QA, multi-hop retrieval) and to stale/contradictory information (Selective Forgetting via FactConsolidation). For SF, explicit prompt guardrails are added (facts indexed by serial numbers; 'newer facts have larger serial numbers'; agents mandated to resolve conflicts by selecting the newest fact). Agentic agents may use self-reflection for noise filtering.
memory_type: The benchmark evaluates multiple memory types: none/full-context buffer (long-context agents, FIFO eviction), episodic external store (RAG agents), graph memory (GraphRAG/HippoRAG-v2/Cognee/Zep), tree memory (RAPTOR), and agentic/multi-component memory (MemGPT, MIRIX, MemoRAG, Self-RAG). It primarily focuses on textual-history and external-database memory (not parametric).
write_back: True (for the evaluated agents). Each ingested chunk is written into the agent's memory during the incremental construction phase (stored as raw text, embeddings, KG nodes/edges, tree nodes, or agentic memory entries). The benchmark mandates that all agents take chunks one by one, absorb them into memory, and incrementally update memory.
online_growth: True. The retrievable store grows during deployment/test-time as chunks are streamed in time order; this incremental accumulation (vs single-block static context) is the central design principle distinguishing memory agents from long-context LLMs.
write_back_trigger: Per-chunk during the memory-construction phase: every incoming chunk triggers a memory write/update. For structure-augmented and agentic systems the write may involve abstraction/consolidation (summarization, KG extraction). Triggers are agent-internal; the benchmark only mandates incremental ingestion of every chunk.
failure_experience_usage: N/A / not modeled. There are no agent task trajectories with success/failure labels stored; the stored content is the ingested context, not the agent's own success/failure experiences. The Selective Forgetting task instead stores both old (now-incorrect) and new (correct) facts, requiring the agent to override outdated information.
memory_evolution_update: Depends on agent: append-only for raw/embedding RAG and long-context (FIFO eviction once window exceeded); refine/consolidate for structure-augmented (RAPTOR recursive summaries, GraphRAG/Zep graph updates) and agentic memory (MemGPT paging, MIRIX). The Selective Forgetting competency specifically probes refine/overwrite/forget behavior, which the benchmark finds all methods handle poorly (multi-hop <=7% accuracy).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/case-selection is fixed similarity top-k (or off-the-shelf agent logic); no RL-optimized or learned retrieval policy is introduced or required by the benchmark.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent (single-user) private memory; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing is evaluated. (MIRIX is internally multi-component/multi-agent memory for one user, but memory is not shared across distinct agents/users in the benchmark.)
benchmarks: MemoryAgentBench (2071 questions, context depth 103K-1.44M tokens). Datasets: Accurate Retrieval - SH-Doc QA (~197K), MH-Doc QA (~421K), LongMemEval(S*) (~355K, reformulated to 5 dialogues/300 questions), EventQA (new, ~534K); Test-Time Learning - BANKING77 (~103K, 77 labels), CLINC150 (151 labels), NLU (68 labels), TREC-Coarse (6 labels), TREC-Fine (50 labels), Movie Recommendation (~1.44M); Long-Range Understanding - infinity-Bench Sum/En.Sum (~172K), Detective QA (~124K, 10 novels/71 questions); Selective Forgetting - FactConsolidation-SH and FactConsolidation-MH (new, ~262K, built from MQUAKE counterfactual edit pairs, context lengths 6K/32K/64K/262K).
benchmark_family: memory (LongMemEval-derived dialogue QA, FactConsolidation) + long-context/QA (infinity-Bench Sum, DetectiveQA, NIAH-style Doc QA) + test-time-learning classification (BANKING77/CLINC150/NLU/TREC) + recommendation (ReDial/movie). It is itself a new memory-agent benchmark family unifying these sources.
baselines: Long-Context Agents: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini (reference backbone), GPT-4.1-mini, Gemini-2.0-Flash, Claude-3.7-Sonnet. Simple RAG: BM25. Embedding RAG: Contriever, OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, text-embedding-3-large, Qwen3-Embedding-4B. Structure-Augmented RAG: RAPTOR, GraphRAG, MemoRAG, HippoRAG-v2, Mem0, Cognee, Zep. Agentic Memory: Self-RAG, MemGPT, MIRIX (and MIRIX with GPT-4.1-mini backbone). Reasoning-model validation: GPT-4o and o4-mini on FactConsolidation. (RAG and commercial memory agents use GPT-4o-mini as default backbone.)
key_metrics: Accuracy (SH-QA, MH-QA, LME(S*), EventQA, MCC classification, Detective QA, FactConsolidation-SH/MH); Recall@5 (Movie Recommendation); F1-Score (infinity-Bench Sum novel summarization). Per-competency averages (AR/TTL/LRU/SF) and an Overall score. Appendix also reports computational latency, GPU memory usage, and cost-performance analysis.
headline_result: No existing memory agent masters all four competencies. Best overall scores are modest: Claude-3.7-Sonnet 49.6 and GPT-4o 48.8 (long-context agents) lead overall. Key splits: RAG agents excel at Accurate Retrieval (HippoRAG-v2 AR Avg 65.1, matching/ beating GPT-4o-mini's 49.2), but long-context models dominate Test-Time Learning and Long-Range Understanding. Selective Forgetting is a universal failure: all methods achieve at most ~7% on multi-hop FactConsolidation (FC-MH), and only long-context agents reach reasonable single-hop scores (GPT-4o 60.0 FC-SH). Even o4-mini drops from 80.0 to 14.0 on FC-MH as context grows from 6K to 32K.
ablations: (1) Input chunk size: smaller chunks + more retrieval calls help Accurate Retrieval (especially embedding RAG) but hurt Long-Range Understanding (RAG ill-suited to coherent global context). (2) Retrieval top-k (2/5/10): larger k generally improves performance; k=10 at 4096 chunk size already ~40K tokens, so k=20 not evaluated. (3) Backbone model (GPT-4o-mini / GPT-4.1-mini / Gemini-2.0-Flash): for RAG agents a sufficiently strong backbone is no longer the bottleneck (marginal gains), but for agentic memory (MIRIX) a stronger backbone gives large gains (Avg 15.9 -> 25.6, +9.7; overall 26.2 -> 37.7). (4) FactConsolidation validation with reasoning models (GPT-4o, o4-mini) shows the dataset is solvable in short context (o4-mini FC-MH 6K = 80.0) but breaks at longer context (32K = 14.0), confirming task validity and that the bottleneck is long-range reasoning over memory.
evaluation_decoupling: Largely coupled to end-to-end task metrics (accuracy/F1/Recall@5 per competency). Intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG over chunks) are not the primary reported scores; the benchmark measures downstream answer correctness, though chunk-size and top-k ablations indirectly probe retrieval quality. Recall@5 is used as the recommendation task metric rather than as a retriever-intrinsic metric.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (final-answer accuracy/F1/Recall@5). Process quality is examined indirectly via ablations (chunk size, top-k, backbone, context-length scaling) and the FactConsolidation validation, but no per-step reasoning-faithfulness or trajectory-quality score is reported.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported in appendices: computational latency analysis, GPU memory usage comparison, and a cost-performance estimation (Appendix I). Practical cost choices noted in main text: chunk size 4096 uniformly used for Mem0/Cognee/Zep/MIRIX due to API cost; top-k=20 not evaluated due to ~40K-token input cost; associating one large (up to 1M-token) context with many questions is preferred over one-question-per-context for efficiency. Specific dollar/latency numbers are in appendices [uncertain on exact values].
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k retrieval: default top-k=10 chunks (ablated 2/5/10). Chunk size 512 for AR (SH/MH-Doc QA, LME(S*)) and all SF tasks; 4096 for other tasks and uniformly for commercial memory agents. With 4096-token chunks and k=10, injected context ~40K tokens. Long-context agents use a FIFO buffer capped at the model's window (128K-1M+), evicting earliest chunks when exceeded.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (benchmark, not a survey). Organizing axes are the four memory competencies (Accurate Retrieval, Test-Time Learning, Long-Range Understanding, Selective Forgetting) crossed with three agent categories (Long-Context Agents, RAG Agents [Simple/Embedding/Structure-Augmented], Agentic Memory Agents). References: 84.
benchmark_construction_and_size: 2071 questions; context depth 103K-1.44M tokens. Construction: reconstructs existing long-context datasets into incremental multi-turn chunk streams, plus two new LLM/automated-pipeline datasets - EventQA (fully automated pipeline over novels; multiple-choice event selection) and FactConsolidation (built from MQUAKE counterfactual edit pairs ordered old->new). LongMemEval reformulated to LME(S*) = 5 dialogues / 300 questions. Answer verifiability: mostly exact-match/multiple-choice accuracy, Recall@5 for recommendation, F1 for summarization. Difficulty signal: best overall system ~49.6 (Claude-3.7-Sonnet); Selective Forgetting multi-hop maxes at ~7% for evaluated memory agents (validated as solvable in short context by o4-mini at 80.0 on FC-MH 6K).
builds_on: Reconstructs / builds on prior datasets: LongMemEval, infinity-Bench (En.Sum), DetectiveQA, MQUAKE (counterfactual edits for FactConsolidation), BANKING77/CLINC150/NLU/TREC (test-time-learning classification), ReDial / conversational movie recommendation, NIAH-style document QA. Conceptually grounded in memory/cognitive science (James 1890; McClelland et al. 1995; Anderson & Neely 1996; Wimber et al. 2015) and the in-context-learning-as-test-time-learning line (Bertsch et al. 2024; HELMET/Yen et al. 2024).
contrasts_with: Positioned against prior memory/long-context benchmarks that cover only subsets of competencies and use shorter/static contexts: MemoryBank, LoCoMo (~9-10K), PerLTQA, RealTalk, LongMemEval, StoryBench, and long-context benchmarks (LongBench, LooGLE, infinity-Bench, RULER, HELMET, NOCHA, NoLiMa, NovelQA, Loong) and RAG benchmarks (KILT, BEIR, RAGBench, etc.). MemoryAgentBench is the only one covering all four competencies (AR/TTL/LRU/SF) and all three agent categories (LCA/RAG/AM) with incremental multi-turn injection.
lineage: Surveys/benchmarks line of the retrieval-augmented agents map: a memory-agent evaluation benchmark (group: surveys). Sits alongside memory benchmarks like LongMemEval and LoCoMo, extending them to a unified four-competency, incremental-multi-turn protocol spanning long-context, RAG, and agentic-memory architectures.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool-retrieval engineering; not a tool-use benchmark).
index_content_separation: N/A. No lightweight-index-then-content / progressive-disclosure separation is prescribed; RAG agents store and retrieve full chunks. (Structure-augmented agents implicitly separate KG/summary indices from source text, but this is per-agent, not a benchmark design.)
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A. Memory is built from a streamed conversation, not from a live/external tool index; no RapidAPI/REST/MCP tool protocol involved. Some agents use function-calling internally (e.g., MemGPT memory operations), but no tool-API store is benchmarked.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no inter-tool dependency modeling; not a tool-use benchmark).
